rulings.docket_item: C5 label outlier from peer_c28's new finding (row P11-066, span Prov.27.23-Prov.27.27, C5): typed admonition_unit -- the sole admonition_unit among all 121 C5 rows per the peer's census; its OL imperative-pair challenge upheld on morphological grounds; the peer proposed relabel to proverb_cluster for boss adoption. Under the B-8 operative-category precedent: does the span carry the admonition form on its own bytes (label stands, outlier status = texture), or do the bytes fail the form test (adopt the label correction)?
rulings.decision: The admonition_unit label STANDS on P11-066 -- the span's bytes genuinely carry the admonition form, so the label is a per-bytes application of the closed vocabulary deviating from C5's single-proverb default, exactly as the B-8 operative-category precedent permits; peer_c28's proposed relabel to proverb_cluster is DECLINED (it would be byte-false); the census outlier status is texture. Disclosure cure ordered, integrating the two standing peer cures with a new deviation disclosure.
rulings.grounds: Form test re-derived from the spliced bytes (byte tier; NO staged morphology layer exists for this book, so verb-form identifications are argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, per TOOLKIT -- the same footing as peer_c28's upheld OL parse, independently re-walked here). oshb:Prov.27.23 (7 words): word 1 יָדֹ֣עַ is the Qal infinitive absolute of the root ידע; word 2 תֵּ֭דַע is the Qal imperfect 2ms of the same root -- together the infinitive-absolute-plus-cognate-imperfect emphatic construction, injunctive in force and rendered as commands in both cola by the English witness -- “Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,” (web:Prov.27.23); word 5 שִׁ֥ית (skeleton שית) is the Qal imperative 2ms with the 2ms-suffixed object לִ֝בְּךָ֗ -- the span's ONE true morphological imperative. oshb:Prov.27.24 opens verse-initial כִּ֤י governing a verbless negative motive clause לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן -- “for riches are not forever,” (web:Prov.27.24) -- dependent on v23's command, not an independent saying. oshb:Prov.27.25 carries three third-person verbs, גָּלָ֣ה / וְנִרְאָה / וְ֝נֶאֶסְפ֗וּ -- descriptive premise, no second-person form; vv26-27 are verbless nominal clauses. The 2ms addressee suffix frame (skeleton tier, 1-based word positions): צאנך + לבך (v23 words 4/6), ללבושך (v26 word 2), ללחמך + ביתך + לנערותיך (v27 words 4/6/8) -- the addressee brackets the span while v24 hangs on its verse-initial motive particle and v25 supplies the ecological premise for the v26-27 yield list. VERDICT ON THE FORM TEST: one true 2ms imperative plus an emphatic injunction, a verse-initial motive clause, and a result list under a bracketing 2ms frame IS the admonition form (imperatives + motive clauses) carried on the span's own bytes -- B-8's mood test (governing second-person imperative frame: the frame structures the span, v24's motive and the v26-27 yield list hang off the v23 command) fires; the row's defect is its WORDING ('2ms imperative pair', already killed by the upheld OL challenge), not its label. THE LAW: under the B-8 controlling precedent, Section 6 legislates exclusivity only where it says so. The C2+C5 line's modal terms are SINGLE_PROVERB DEFAULT and proverb_cluster ONLY with named cohesion: the DEFAULT is overridable per bytes, and the ONLY attaches to proverb_cluster's evidence bar -- inflating the pair into a two-value exhaustive grant for C5 inserts an ONLY the owner did not write, the exact move B-8 rejected for C3. The peer's proposed relabel to proverb_cluster fails on this span's own bytes: proverb_cluster asserts multiple independently complete sayings bound by cohesion, but v24 is a dependent motive clause and v25 a dependent premise -- a command-motive-support-result chain is ONE instruction, and a STRUCTURAL vocabulary cannot demand a byte-false label (B-8). B-8's identical-construction principle seals it: imperative-plus-motive spans in C3 are typed admonition_unit, and the same structural shape cannot carry a different structural type merely for sitting in C5. CENSUS (re-derived, row-count unit, combined corpus): 121 C5 rows = 110 single_proverb / 10 proverb_cluster / 1 admonition_unit, P11-066 the sole admonition_unit -- digits match peer_c28 exactly. Outlier status is a fact about label DISTRIBUTION across rows, not about this span's bytes; by owner-addendum symmetry (absence/rarity is never counterevidence) it is texture obliging disclosure, never grounds for relabel. (B-10's adoption shifts the census to 111/9/1 without touching this ruling.)

rulings.docket_item: peer_c27 escalation (row P11-035, span Prov.26.18-Prov.26.19, C5): a grammatically continuous single sentence spanning two verses, 0/560 corpus precedent either way under the closed 8-value vocabulary. Decide the application: proverb_cluster with the syntax as the named cohesion evidence, or single_proverb read as one proverb-unit independent of verse count; state the ruling as decision-local precedent for the corpus and specify the row's cure.
rulings.decision: ADOPT the unit_type change: P11-035 becomes single_proverb over the unchanged span Prov.26.18-Prov.26.19 (peer_c27's LF challenge upheld in substance; the escalation is resolved without owner referral). RULED READING, decision-local precedent for the corpus: single_proverb names one proverb-UNIT independent of verse count; a grammatically continuous single sentence spanning adjacent verses is ONE proverb, and syntactic continuation is not proverb_cluster cohesion evidence, because the cluster category presupposes multiple independently complete sayings.
rulings.grounds: Bytes first (every Hebrew run spliced from verse_map_oshb.json / consonantal_index.json; 1-based word positions). oshb:Prov.26.18 is 5 words -- כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ (comparison particle prefixed to a participle, 'like a madman') + הַיֹּרֶ֥ה (article + participle, 'who shoots') + three bare nouns -- no finite predicate for a human referent and no apodosis; oshb:Prov.26.19 opens with verse-initial כֵּֽן (word 1) followed by אִ֭ישׁ, supplying the pair's sole apodosis: one grammatically continuous sentence -- “Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,” (web:Prov.26.18) “is the man who deceives his neighbor” (web:Prov.26.19). Comparanda re-derived (skeleton tier, word-bound token כן, word positions): 26:1 word 5, 26:2 word 5, 26:8 word 4, 27:8 word 5, 27:19 word 4 -- every other comparative simile in the part completes protasis and ken-apodosis inside ONE verse, while 26:18 carries no כן at all; the row's facts hold (peer-verified, re-derived here). THE APPLICATION IS RESOLVABLE -- no owner escalation -- because three gate grounds converge on single_proverb: (1) The C2+C5 law is modal: SINGLE_PROVERB DEFAULT; proverb_cluster ONLY with byte-grounded cohesion NAMED. Cohesion is glue BETWEEN sayings: every cluster-evidence class the owner names (the 26:4-5 answer/answer-not pair, catchword chains, the 15:33-16:9 YHWH cluster, the kings run, tov-min construction runs) binds multiple independently complete sayings -- peer_c27's verified reading of the section text, confirmed against the strategy. Prov.26.18-19 contains exactly ONE saying; there are no member sayings to cohere, so the cluster bar cannot be met even in principle -- and where the ONLY-bar cannot engage, the modally binding DEFAULT holds over its own object, the proverb-UNIT. The 'strongest possible cohesion' reading fails at the object level: syntactic continuation is not cohesion between sayings, it is the absence of a second saying. (2) proverb_cluster would be byte-false on this span: the label asserts plural sayings where the bytes carry one sentence, and a STRUCTURAL vocabulary cannot demand byte-false labels (B-8). (3) Tier-4 discipline: chapter/verse numbers are tier-4 metadata, never evidence. The ka...ken comparative at 26:1 wears single_proverb; 26:18-19 is the same construction class differing ONLY in where the versification splits it -- under B-8's identical-construction principle a structural type cannot turn on a tier-4 accident. PRECEDENT DIGIT (re-derived, row-count unit): 0 of 560 corpus rows carry single_proverb over a multi-verse span, matching peer_c27 -- so the RULED READING is stated as decision-local precedent for the corpus: single_proverb names one proverb-unit independent of verse count; it may span verses ONLY where the span is one grammatically continuous sentence and the rationale names the first verse's incompleteness and the second verse's resolving syntax as the ATOMICITY evidence. SYMMETRY SWEEP over the systemic class touched (all 38 multi-verse proverb_cluster rows' prose, swept for member-incompleteness claims): exactly ONE row claims a member verse is grammatically incomplete alone -- P11-035 itself; the near matches assert dependency between COMPLETE sayings (e.g. the particle opening 19:7 leaning on 19:6's claim at P08-055), which remains genuine cluster cohesion, not sentence-splitting -- the class has one member and this adoption completes it.
